argument_uniqueness_tracing.installment_number: 7 = hand-over next installment 7 + 0. Covered amount = 1490.00 received - 197.00 returned - 114.00 down payment + the type's partial_payment_tolerance_usd 5.00 (base: an installment counts as paid within the type's tolerance; installment 4 was 3.00 short) = 1184.00; 1184.00 / 197.00 = 6.01 -> 6 whole installments -> next installment 7. Installment 7 is the returned one; after the re-dating it is the schedule anchor installment (anchor date 2026-10-14). Day count: account_closed return -> calendar days, 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-14 = 5. edges.condition: plan_installments carries a plan_schedule_change_recorded row with change_type due_date_change for the installment_number of the plan's latest plan_installment_returned row.
edges.policy_source: The first installment a newly authorized payment method collects is fixed only after the plan's installment history carries a due-date change for the installment of its most recent returned installment payment.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The plan's only return (installment 7, account_closed, 2026-10-07) has no due-date change after it: the installment history holds no plan_schedule_change_recorded row at all, and the plan record's schedule anchor is still installment 1 on 2026-04-06, so installment 7 still carries its original, already passed due date 2026-10-06.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The re-dating write records a due_date_change row for installment 7 (due 2026-10-14) and sets schedule_anchor_installment = 7, schedule_anchor_date = 2026-10-14, final_due_date = 2027-02-14; the hand-over then finds installment 7 as the anchor 5 calendar days out and returns 7 instead of 8.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the re-dating must land before the authorization because the hand-over reads the schedule anchor the re-dating writes; replayed in the reverse order the authorization would carry installment_number 8 (and the record's first due date 2026-11-06), a different terminal state, so only the topological order reproduces gold.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the re-dating write leaves schedule_anchor_installment = 1, so the hand-over's returned installment 7 is not the anchor and the result moves from 7 to 8 (verify.py: with=7 skipped=8); the terminal state also lacks the due_date_change row and keeps installment 7 due 2026-10-06 and final_due_date 2027-02-06.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to move the plan's installments to the debit card; it never mentions a returned or bounced payment, a missed installment, moving or changing a due date, or any re-dating; it reacts to a new date for the October installment only after the agent proposes it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: authorize_payment_method_50f022be reads the plan only to look up the scheduled due date of the installment it is given and then writes the funding_method_change row and rewrites funding_method/authorization_date/authorization_method; it never checks whether a due-date change exists, the plan status or any notice, and returns a normal receipt for any installment number. redate_returned_installment_ce690b15 likewise writes the change for whatever installment and shift it is given.

user_scenario:
You are Thaddeus Quilliam-Oyelaran, forty, a shift supervisor at a distribution warehouse in Westerville, Ohio, calling Ridgeline Recovery Associates on your lunch break. You set up a monthly payment plan with them this spring on an old Lakeshore Federal credit card balance, and the installments have always been taken automatically from your checking account. You open plainly: "Hi, I have a payment plan with you, and I want the payments to come out of my debit card automatically every month from now on." That is all you ask for; you have no idea how the plan is set up on their side and you don't bring up anything else about it.
You give your details only as the agent asks for them, one at a time: your phone number is 614-555-2417, which you say as 6145552417 if they want just the digits; if they need more, the last four of your Social Security number are 2683, and your ZIP code is 43081. Your date of birth, if asked, is July 23, 1986. You don't remember any account or plan numbers and let the agent look them up.
Only if the agent asks why you want the change, you explain that you moved your paycheck to a new bank and closed the old checking account last week, so nothing should go to that account anymore. If asked which card, it is your Visa debit card from the new bank, ending in 2290. You never use e-mail and you will not sign anything online; if the agent mentions an electronic signature, you say you would rather just give your OK right here on this recorded call.
If the agent tells you that something on the plan has to be adjusted first so the card can take over, you say that is fine with you and let them go ahead; you don't ask about it yourself. When the agent says they are passing the authorization over for you to complete yourself and gives you what to enter, you do it exactly as they tell you, with the values they read out, and if they ask you can repeat back what the confirmation shows. If the agent mentions the installment amount of 197 dollars, that matches what you remember paying.
Once the agent tells you the debit card is set up for the automatic payments, you thank them and say goodbye.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (payment_arrangement_servicing, category plan).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [4, 4]; redating policy takes 4 factors, hand-over policy takes 4.
[Step 0 scope] Nothing claimed before (task 0). Asset ledger finding that shaped the whole difficulty: plan_installment_paid / plan_installment_returned trigger account events and plan_authorized / plan_broken / plan_reinstated trigger account:account_arrangement_opened/closed, so no task tool may write them (principle D); the writable plan events are plan_schedule_change_recorded (due-date change, restructure, deferral, payment-method change, each rewriting the plan record), plan_installment_missed, plan_resumed, plan_suspended, plan_cancelled/plan_balance_released. The customer's own acts in this category are the authorization of a new payment method and the authorization of recurring debits / stated income for a restructure. Task 0 claims the payment-method change (owner=user, root) and the due-date change used to re-date a returned installment (agent, prerequisite). Reserved for task 1 (independent tree): restructure (owner=user root), resumption after a hardship suspension, missed-installment recording and a deferral - four writes and four computations nobody here touches.
[Design thesis] Surface goal: 'move my plan payments to my debit card automatically'. Core scored value: installment_number on the consumer's payment-method authorization = the first installment the new card collects (7). Hidden hop: the October installment's ACH debit came back for a closed account (never presented again) and its due date (2026-10-06) has passed, so the hand-over rule's first installment is fixed only after that installment has been re-dated by a due-date change; the re-dating shift (8 days) is itself a 4-factor calculation. Depth: surface -> prerequisite sentence -> returned installment found on the installment history -> re-dating policy -> shift -> plan record rewritten -> hand-over computed on the rewritten anchor. Breadth: payment record (paid count, returns in 12 months, missed entries), return reason and timing, payment channel, the placed account's returns (account category), card history on the consumer's accounts (account category), the plan's funding method and the type's tolerance / max shift / grace.
[Problem-tree card] root plan_ext_new_method_handover (target authorize_payment_method_50f022be, owner=user) <- plan_ext_returned_installment_redating (target redate_returned_installment_ce690b15, owner=agent). Edge kind value_input, gate binding result (reads schedule_anchor_installment), form state. Prerequisite sentence (in the root's own rule, affirmative direction, the way a desk states that a figure waits on a record): "The first installment a newly authorized payment method collects is fixed only after the plan's installment history carries a due-date change for the installment of its most recent returned installment payment." Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state (a due-date change entry on the installment history for a named installment), no actor or tool; no tool name, policy id or snake_case token; strength 'only after' = hard, scope = exactly the installment of the most recent return. Uniqueness of the resolving write: within this difficulty only the re-dating policy writes change_type due_date_change (restructure, deferral, payment-method change and the other writes carry other change types or other events), so sentence + records (installment 7 returned, no change entry) + the re-dating rule ('the installment that payment was for is re-dated by one due-date change') lead to exactly one action. Seed evidence it is false at the opening: plan_installments has no plan_schedule_change_recorded row; payment_plans.bfd361fc-a9a6-4fa7-b33a-aa11c7086b17.schedule_anchor_installment = 1 and schedule_anchor_date = 2026-04-06; the return row 97545112-c374-4ff2-88f6-7706b5d2f8d6 (installment 7, account_closed, received 2026-10-07). It flips true when the re-dating write lands (anchor 7 / 2026-10-14). Deletion sensitivity (verify.py): skipping the re-dating changes the hand-over from 7 to 8 and removes the change row, so the edge bears weight. Topological order: re-dating (step 7) before authorization (step 9). No parallel edges. user_scenario never mentions a returned payment, a missed installment or a date change; the tools validate nothing (they write whatever installment/shift/method they are given).
[Base-invariant card] Write subject plan_schedule_change_recorded for both calls. Governing base policies: plan_evt_schedule_changes (gate change_on_active_plan: 'Schedule and payment-method changes are granted only on a plan whose status is active.' evidence payment_plans.bfd361fc-a9a6-4fa7-b33a-aa11c7086b17.status = active, correlated by plan_id) and plan_agg_combined_affordability (no eligibility gate for this subject; budget_review_required is false for a Standard Installment Plan, so no affordability test). Inherited, unchanged: due-date change limited to due_date_change_max_per_12_months (2; none used), shift at most due_date_change_max_shift_days (15; 8 used), monthly due day kept on or before 28 (new day 14); payment-method changes limited to funding_change_max_per_12_months (2; none used), card_autopay_allowed true and 197.00 <= card_autopay_max_installment_usd 2000.00; recorded oral authorization allowed for the type (plan_evt_authorization), the consumer's own act. plan_evt_installments: 'returns for account_closed, stop_payment, unauthorized_debit and card_chargeback are never presented again' (why re-dating rather than re-presentment); grace_period_days_autopay 5 counted from the 2026-10-06 due date runs through 2026-10-11, so at frozen_time 2026-10-09 the installment is not yet missed (positive case: handling 2026-10-12 would make the miss owed; boundary 2026-10-11 still within grace) - so no missed-installment obligation is lit in this world. No time-kind eligibility gate governs these writes, hence temporal_feasibility is empty.
[Business-object card] Target object: payment plan bfd361fc-a9a6-4fa7-b33a-aa11c7086b17 on placed account 8baf17d2-6504-4950-a43e-641c0248516a; correlation key plan_id. Rows aggregated: the plan's 8 plan_installment_paid rows (installments 0-7), 1 plan_installment_returned row (installment 7, source a17e4ae2-97df-4403-bb9a-fc96f34a5299), no missed rows, no change rows; account_transactions of the consumer for the cross reads (the 150.00 check paid outside the plan 2026-02-10 and returned for stop_payment 2026-02-17; the account mirror of the installment-7 return, excluded from the buffer because it carries plan_id; debit_card payment 2026-07-02). Excluded: the account_balance_placed row and the 200.00 check payment of 2026-01-15 made before the plan existed (no plan_id) - they do not enter any plan aggregate; the check payment is not a card payment.
[Factor card - re-dating shift (expected 8, baseline_result 10)] (1) redating_lead_by_payment_record, parameter, multi-source: paid count 7 (8 payments - 1 return) >= 6 AND 0 other returns in 12 months -> 3 days (fall-through 7 -> 14). (2) redating_clock_start_by_return, method: account_closed return received 1 day after due (<= 5) -> clock starts 2026-10-07 (fall-through handling date -> 10). (3) redating_day_count_by_channel, method: ach_bank_debit -> business days; 5 business days after Wed 2026-10-07 = Wed 2026-10-14, 7 calendar days (fall-through calendar -> 6). (4) redating_buffer_by_account_returns, parameter, cross-difficulty (account): one payment made outside any plan and returned in 6 months (check_by_mail 150.00 of 2026-02-10, returned 2026-02-17 for stop_payment) -> 2 days (fall-through 0 -> 6); the account mirror of the plan's own installment-7 return carries plan_id and is excluded (near-miss). Near-miss: the 2026-01-15 payment on the account is not a return and is outside the plan; the plan's single return is the one being re-dated, so it is excluded from 'other returns'.
[Factor card - hand-over installment (expected 7, baseline_result 8)] The covered amount uses the type's partial_payment_tolerance_usd exactly as base plan_evt_installments does (5.00 for a Standard plan; installment 4 short 3.00 counts as covered); tolerance is no longer a factor.
